newsitem.title: FRANCE: Axa denies talk it plans UAP buy.
newsitem.headline: Axa denies talk it plans UAP buy.

text.p: A spokeswoman for French insurance company Axa SA denied on Wednesday market rumours that it was planning a takeover of rival Unions des Assurances de Paris (UAP).
"Axa denies the rumours, according to which it is making a public offer for UAP," the spokeswoman said.
The rumours sent UAP shares higher in the afternoon, while Axa lost ground. UAP closed up 3.30 francs at 103.50, while Axa ended down 1.60 francs at 283.90.
Takeover rumours have stalked UAP since the beginning of the year, due to the weakness of its shares. The insurance firm was privatised in May 1994 at 152 francs per share to small investors.

Financial newsletter La Lettre de l'Expansion said in its latest edition that rumours of a takeover of UAP by Axa were fed by news that three investment banks had written three studies on the benefits of a takeover and have made it known. wem/pnt
